findings.claim: The manifesto now points at a test that no longer exists and still calls I11 planned. I10 cites test_minio_backup_syncs_a_declared_bucket, which the change renamed to test_minio_backup_syncs_declared_buckets. I11 says 'planned' and that the ticket 'widens the job', but this change built it and test_minio_backup_syncs_the_durable_buckets now enforces it. .okf/summary.md lines 69-70 also say the backup jobs 'do not have yet' a copy of every durable bucket.

Several pages still say only openviking is backed up, or describe this ticket as future work. In .okf/components/gcs-backups.md the 'Planned, not built' section describes this ticket as unbuilt. Its 180-day trap quotes the reference page as calling the rule 'a safety net for orphaned objects', a sentence this change removed. 'The marker flags fix that from the next run' is also out of date, since the run has happened. The same claim is in .okf/components/minio.md:141 ('Only one bucket is backed up'), .okf/components/container-registry.md:114 ('Not backed up'), .okf/nodes/orangepi4a.md:127, docs/how-to/run-a-backup-job-on-demand.md:65 ('syncs the openviking bucket') and the generated line in .okf/components/index.md:15, which kmctl check --fix regenerates.

SYNC_LINE matches only the exact 'rclone sync minio:X gcs:${gcs_bucket}/minio/Y/ ...' shape, and every check iterates over its matches. A fifth sync in another shape is invisible to the set-equality check, as are a sync with the flags before the destination or one that is not the last command on its line. The same goes for a bucket copied with 'rclone copy'. Count every 'rclone (sync|copy)' occurrence in the args and assert it equals the number of SYNC_LINE matches, so an unmatched command fails the test instead of slipping past it.
